subject: business-studies
title: PESTLE Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll meet PESTLE — political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies external influences — the PESTLE framework explained.
final_note: You can list and define each PESTLE factor and give a real example of each.

concepts.def: Government policy and stability affecting business
New tech that creates or destroys markets
Laws on employment, consumers, the environment

walkthroughs.body_html:
PESTLE helps firms spot threats and opportunities outside their control.

If they ignore it, they may launch in a shrinking market or break new laws.
P: Brexit changing trade rules. E: rising interest rates. S: ageing population. T: AI tools. L: minimum wage rise. En: single-use plastic bans.
Firms react by adjusting strategy: cut costs in a recession, invest in tech to stay competitive, switch suppliers to meet new laws.

options: Political
Economic
Social
Legal

options: Technological
Environmental
Legal
Social

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.

mcqs.q: What do McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y describe?
options: Two contrasting management assumptions: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control; Theory Y assumes workers can be self-motivated and seek responsibility.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
Theory X is about working in a factory and Theory Y is about office work.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
